title: Security discovery: TesseraWare identity & logs
summary: Introductory security discovery focusing on SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit log retention and format, and encryption/KMS options. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private for data residency and BYOK; interested in SOC2 artifacts and a follow-up deep dive on KMS/HSM flow and audit log export. Agreed next steps around sending compliance docs, architecture diagram, and scheduling a SE-led bench test for logging throughput.
topics: SSO / SAML integration and IdP support
RBAC and least-privilege model for API keys and console
Audit logging schema, retention, and export (SIEM integration)
Encryption options: Redwood KMS vs BYOK, HSM support
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for data residency and latency
SOC 2 / ISO27001 evidence and compliance matrix
Next steps: SOC2 docs, diagram, bench test scheduling

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-31 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Bell (Redwood SE), Asha Rao (CTO - TesseraWare), Benji Marshall (Security Lead), Sofia Ruiz (Platform Engineer)

Summary (auto-generated): Quick intro, customer's current stack (Okta, Splunk), major concerns around data residency and key ownership, desire for audit log export and clear retention SLA. Redwood explained Hosted/Dedicated/Private tradeoffs and BYOK paths.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick round-robin?
[00:07] Asha Rao: hi, i'm asha. we're the cto, i run platform and infra. looking to understand how you'd fit into our security posture.
[00:14] Benji Marshall: hey, benji here, security lead. main worries are keys, logs and retention, and how we can prove compliance for auditors.
[00:22] Sofia Ruiz: sofia, platform. i'll likely run any pilot and run the bench tests.
[00:30] Lena Park: great thanks. Marcus from our infra team will go into the technical bits. Marcus?
[00:36] Marcus Bell: hey all, quick agenda: SSO and RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS options and BYOK, then deployment modes. i'll try to keep it concrete.

[02:12] Asha Rao: short context — we use Okta, SAML. we want SSO for console and API accounts. also need role-based access so devs can't spin up prod models.
[02:30] Marcus Bell: totally. Redwood supports SAML SSO, SSO for console plus token provisioning. our RBAC lets you map SAML groups to roles; you can also do fine-grained API key scopes per route. one caveat: the provisioning flow differs slightly between Hosted and Private — with Hosted we support SCIM for group sync, with Private you can opt for 2-way LDAP if you run on-prem.
[03:05] Benji Marshall: SCIM is good, but we need proof of group sync timing. auditors ask about time to revoke access. how fast can we revoke a user token?
[03:20] Marcus Bell: for Hosted, token revocation via our control plane is near realtime — typically sub-60s for control-plane driven revocations. for Dedicated if you enable local auth caching it's sub-5 minutes worst case, and Private can be sync-with-your-idp immediate if you host the auth flow locally. there are caveats with long-lived API keys; we recommend short-lived tokens + refresh for sensitive roles.
[04:10] Sofia Ruiz: okay that helps. question on RBAC: can we limit model access per team and also per-environment? like team-A only has access to gpt-large-prod models, dev team gets smaller sandbox models.
[04:26] Marcus Bell: yes, policies support per-route and per-model scoping. you can bind SAML groups or LDAP groups to policies. small note — model variants may have different endpoints so policy mapping is per endpoint.

[06:00] Asha Rao: logs — we use Splunk. need audit trail for user actions, API calls, model inputs/outputs maybe redacted. how does Redwood retain and export logs?
[06:18] Lena Park: we capture audit logs for admin actions, model request metadata, and security events. full request/response payload storage is configurable and for privacy you can choose to redact PII at ingestion. export options: streaming to customer SIEM (syslog/HTTPS), S3 export, or push to our private VPC endpoint. retention is policy-driven.
[06:55] Benji Marshall: retention policy question — we have a 7-year retention requirement for certain PII for auditing; can we put logs into cold storage and hold that long? also chain of custody?
[07:14] Marcus Bell: yes cold storage to S3 (or your GCS) is supported. we can set lifecycle policies for transition to Glacier. chain of custody: we attach ingestion timestamps and immutable write-once WORM-like options if needed; for Hosted we have a tamper-evident log path and we provide digests for integrity checks. for Private you manage storage directly so chain of custody is under your control.
[08:05] Sofia Ruiz: what's the format for logs? Splunk friendly?
[08:12] Marcus Bell: JSON lines, timestamps in ISO, fields include user_id, request_id, model, token_count, latency_ms, event_type. we can provide a mapping doc to Splunk sourcetypes. sometimes the transcriber might call it "K-V cash" in notes but it's KV cache.

[10:00] Asha Rao: encryption — our policy is BYOK for keys in production. we run AWS KMS with CloudHSM backed keys. how do you handle encryption at rest and envelope encryption?
[10:18] Marcus Bell: Redwood supports envelope encryption. by default we manage keys but you can opt for BYOK via AWS KMS or an external HSM; we support import / external key references and bring-your-own-key flows. for Dedicated we can set up a customer key that we never persist, we get ephemeral wraps. for Private you integrate directly with your KMS/HSM.
[10:55] Benji Marshall: any FIPS or HSM modules supported?
[11:03] Marcus Bell: we support HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM), and can run FIPS validated modules in Private deployments. Hosted is FIPS-compatible components in our stack but if you need FIPS-certified HSMs or on-prem HSMs we recommend Private.

[13:30] Asha Rao: auditors ask for SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence. do you have the reports and how recent?
[13:40] Lena Park: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II covering security and availability for our Hosted product, and ISO27001 certificate for our control plane. i'll send the redacted reports. for Dedicated/Private we provide a compliance matrix showing shared responsibilities.
[14:05] Benji Marshall: good. will that include pen test summaries and remediation timelines?
[14:12] Lena Park: yes, summarized pen test findings with remediation status. detailed findings we redact PII but can share under NDA if needed.

[16:00] Sofia Ruiz: deployment questions — latency for inference in Dedicated vs Hosted?
[16:08] Marcus Bell: Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs in a region — predictable p99 latency, usually slightly better than multi-tenant Hosted under high load because you have reserved capacity. Hosted is generally lower friction for getting started and scales automatically, but Dedicated is for predictable tail-latency. Private adds network hop otherwise it's local to your VPC so lowest network latency if co-located.
[17:00] Asha Rao: we also have data residency constraints — customer data must remain within EU. do you have EU-only hosting and can you isolate control plane?
[17:14] Lena Park: yes, we have EU regions and a Private control plane option. for strict residency, Private on-prem or VPC-hosted Dedicated in EU region is the recommended path.

[19:30] Benji Marshall: what about audit logs access for auditors? can they query logs or read-only view?
[19:38] Marcus Bell: we support cross-account read-only S3 buckets for auditors, and role-based access to the console for auditor accounts. for Hosted we can provide short-lived credentials scoped to read-only exports.

[22:00] Asha Rao: encryption key lifecycle - rotation, revocation. if we revoke a key what happens to older data?
[22:10] Marcus Bell: old objects remain encrypted with the old key until you re-encrypt; rotation policy can be automatic or manual. for shards that need immediate rekeying we provide a bulk re-encrypt job. note though for massive archives re-encrypt can be long running. we document time estimates.

[25:00] Sofia Ruiz: sample compliance checklist — can you share a matrix that maps your controls to SOC2 sections and our requirements?
[25:10] Lena Park: yes i'll include the matrix. it'll map control owner (redwood vs customer) and evidence location.

[28:00] Benji Marshall: any gotchas for logging request/response bodies? we want to avoid storing PII in logs but need enough context for debugging.
[28:12] Marcus Bell: we can configure request/response redaction at ingestion — regex-based or schema-aware redaction. we also support live redaction pipelines so PII never lands in retention buckets. but remember that some debug cases require full context so we'll give you toggles and audit log of who turned redaction off.

[31:00] Asha Rao: about pricing — does Dedicated include longer retention tiers or is that an add-on?
[31:09] Lena Park: retention longer than default is an add-on; for long-term cold storage we bill based on egress and object storage costs plus a management fee. we'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.

[34:00] Marcus Bell: technical note — for bench testing audit log throughput, we recommend a 24-48hr trial with synthetic load. we'll instrument token_count and log event size and stream to your Splunk endpoint.

[36:45] Sofia Ruiz: timeline — ideally we'd like to have a pilot in Q4 and decision by end of year. security review is blocking.
[36:55] Lena Park: understood. we'll prioritize SOC2 docs and a SE deep dive next week.

[40:00] Benji Marshall: final question: who is responsible if an audit finds a gap in our Dedicated setup?
[40:08] Lena Park: shared responsibility model. we'll map exactly which controls Redwood owns versus TesseraWare. for Dedicated and Private we have a clearer delineation: you control infra and we control runtime. we'll put that in the matrix.

[42:30] Asha Rao: ok, that was helpful. any immediate blockers?
[42:35] Marcus Bell: none from our side. we'll need the Okta metadata and RBAC spreadsheet to prep the SCIM mappings.

[44:00] Lena Park: recap of next steps: send SOC2 + pen test summary, architecture/KMS doc, schedule 90-min deep dive, customer to share Okta metadata and retention policy.
[44:20] Asha Rao: thanks, talk soon.
[44:24] Benji Marshall: thanks everyone.
[44:27] Sofia Ruiz: bye.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, some speaker labels merged), timestamps are approximate.
